blocks.text: **Sustainable development** = 'development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs' (**Brundtland Report, *Our Common Future*, 1987**). Three pillars — **economic, social, environmental** (planet-people-prosperity); core doctrines — **intergenerational & intragenerational equity, precautionary principle, polluter pays, common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR)**. The institutional ladder: **Stockholm 1972** (UNEP born; India's Art 48A/51A(g) followed via the 42nd Amendment) → Brundtland 1987 → **Rio 1992** (Agenda 21; UNFCCC-CBD-UNCCD triplets) → Johannesburg 2002 → **Rio+20 (2012**, 'The Future We Want') → **SDGs 2015 (Agenda 2030: 17 goals, 169 targets)** — with India's localisation: **NITI's SDG India Index**, state indicator frameworks (AP consistently a **front-runner** category state), and district-level dashboards.

rows: Integration of trade, capital, technology, people and ideas across borders — waves: 1990s LPG-era hyper-globalisation → post-2008 slowbalisation → post-COVID **re-globalisation** (friend-shoring, resilient supply chains, digital-services globalisation)
Technology diffusion (solar-cost collapse via global chains), green finance flows, norm export (ESG, Paris architecture), poverty reduction through trade (the great convergence)

Carbon-intensive freight & production offshoring ('pollution havens' — emissions embedded in trade), resource extraction frontiers, homogenised consumption, race-to-the-bottom fears, and **carbon-border frictions (EU CBAM)** hitting developing exporters — the new trade-climate flashpoint

SDG 17's partnership frame; technology transfer & climate finance ($100 bn → NCQG debates), circular-economy trade, **India's positions**: CBDR, per-capita equity, **LiFE (lifestyle for environment)**, International Solar Alliance & CDRI — globalising solutions, not just supply chains

sections.heading: The AP dimension — sustainability on the delta's edge

items: **Exposure**: a 974-km cyclone coast, delta salinity ingress, Kolleru's eutrophication history, Eastern-Ghats mining pressure, urban air-water stress — AP's development runs on climate's frontline.

**Response stack**: renewable leadership (solar parks, wind, the pumped-storage pipeline, green-hydrogen hubs), **APCNF natural farming** (the agro-ecological flagship), mangrove restoration (Coringa/Krishna), zero-based budgeting of ecology? no — rather **SDG institutionalisation** (AP's planning department dashboards; front-runner rankings), Jagananna-to-current-era housing with green norms, and the blue-economy framing of the port build-out (with CRZ discipline as the tension).

**Globalization's AP face**: shrimp-pharma-granite exports tie village economies to world prices (the US anti-dumping duty on shrimp as the teachable episode); Sri City's global factories; Gulf-remittance Rayalaseema; CBAM's future bite on AP's export basket — the state is a **globalisation case study in miniature**.

**The synthesis line**: for AP, sustainability is not a constraint on development but its **precondition** — a cyclone-alley, delta-fed, export-linked economy has no unsustainable path that is not also self-defeating.

sections.heading: 🗺 Deep mastery — sustainable development, measured

items: **Concept & pillars:** Brundtland's definition; the **three pillars (economic, social, environmental)** and the **17 SDGs (2015-30)**; **planetary boundaries** and the doughnut-economics frame.
**Measures:** **SDG India Index (NITI Aayog), Environmental Performance Index, ecological footprint, HDI/IHDI, and green GDP**.
**Instruments:** circular economy, renewable energy, **LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)**, ESG, carbon markets (Energy Conservation Act 2022), and natural-capital accounting.

**AP dimension:** sustainability 'on the ground' — **APCNF natural farming** (world's largest), high renewable-energy potential, coastal/mangrove (Coringa) conservation, and cyclone-resilient development.

prelimsPointers: **SDGs** — 17 goals (2015-30); India tracked by the **NITI Aayog SDG India Index**.
**Coringa** (Godavari estuary) — the second-largest mangrove forest in India.
**Brundtland Commission (1983-87)** — *Our Common Future*; the canonical SD definition.
**Stockholm 1972** → UNEP; India's **42nd Amendment (1976)** inserted Arts **48A & 51A(g)**.
**Rio 1992**: Agenda 21 + the three conventions (**UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD**); **SDGs (2015)**: 17 goals, 169 targets, horizon 2030.
**SDG India Index (NITI Aayog, 2018–)** — AP has ranked in the **front-runner** band in successive editions.
**CBAM** — the EU's carbon border adjustment (transitional 2023, definitive 2026): the trade-climate flashpoint.
**Mission LiFE (2022)**, **International Solar Alliance (2015)**, **CDRI (2019)** — India's global-solutions triad.
Doctrines: **precautionary principle & polluter pays** absorbed into Indian law via **Vellore Citizens (1996)**; **public trust** via *M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997)*.
mainsAngles: Define sustainable development's pillars and doctrines, and trace the Stockholm-to-SDG institutional ladder.

Common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities — the equity keystone of climate governance.
Where threats of serious harm exist, scientific uncertainty must not postpone preventive action — Indian law via Vellore (1996).
The post-2008 deceleration and reconfiguration of global integration — regionalised, security-conscious supply chains.

sections.heading: The weather machine — temperature, humidity, clouds, winds

rows: Insolation drivers (latitude, altitude, continentality, currents, aspect); **lapse rate ~6.5°C/km**; **inversions** (valley frost, urban smog lids)
Heat budget: ~51% surface absorption; albedo (fresh snow ~80-90%); India's heatwave criteria (IMD: plains ≥40°C + departure norms)
Absolute vs **relative humidity**; dew point; saturation & condensation (dew, frost, fog, mist)
RH highest at dawn; warm air holds more vapour (~7%/°C — Clausius-Clapeyron: the climate-extremes multiplier)
Genera by height: **cirrus (high), alto- (mid), stratus/nimbus (low), cumulonimbus (vertical)**; okta scale (0-8)
**Cumulonimbus = thunderstorm-hail-tornado factory**; nimbostratus = steady rain; cloud radiative double role (day cooling, night blanket)
Pressure-gradient force + **Coriolis** (right-deflection NH) + friction; **geostrophic** balance aloft

Planetary system: trades-westerlies-polar easterlies; ITCZ migration = monsoon's engine; **jet streams** (subtropical, polar; the **tropical easterly jet** in India's monsoon); local winds — land-sea breeze, mountain-valley, **loo, mango showers, Kalbaisakhi**

sections.heading: Special weather phenomena — the exam set

items: **Monsoon mechanics** (the Indian centrepiece): differential heating + ITCZ's northward march + **Mascarene High → Somali (Findlater) jet → moisture surge**; upper-air players — subtropical westerly jet's withdrawal north of the Himalaya, **tropical easterly jet**, Tibetan heating; variability drivers — **ENSO (El Niño ↔ weak monsoon tendency), IOD (positive ↔ favourable), MJO pulses**; breaks and active spells; withdrawal's rain gift to AP (the **northeast/retreating monsoon, Oct-Dec — Rayalaseema & south-coastal AP's second season**).

**Cyclones** (tropical): warm SST ≥26.5°C, low shear, Coriolis beyond ~5° — structure (eye, eyewall, spiral bands); Bay of Bengal's October-November clustering; **naming by WMO/ESCAP panel**; storm surge as the killer arm (full disaster treatment G-091/092). **Temperate (extra-tropical) cyclones**: frontal, larger, west-to-east — **western disturbances** watering rabi Punjab and snowing the Himalaya.

**Thunderstorms & tornadoes**: convective trinity (moisture, instability, lift); India's **Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers)**; hailstorms of the Deccan; lightning as India's biggest single weather killer (~2,500+ deaths/yr) — an under-quoted fact. **El Niño/La Niña & teleconnections**: the Walker-circulation see-saw — one paragraph every examiner expects.

**AP's weather personality**: the **rain-shadow paradox** — SW monsoon's modest yield in Rayalaseema (leeward of the Western Ghats) vs the **NE monsoon's cyclone-laden generosity**; loo-less but heatwave-prone coastal plains (Vizianagaram-Prakasam June spikes); the Bay's October machine aiming at Nellore-Machilipatnam-Kalingapatnam — geography's explanation of AP's farm calendar and disaster calendar alike.

sections.heading: 🗺 Deep mastery — the weather machine & special phenomena

items: **Elements:** temperature, pressure, humidity, wind, precipitation; **insolation, lapse rate, inversion, and atmospheric circulation (Hadley/Ferrel/Polar cells, jet streams)**.

**The Indian monsoon:** the seasonal reversal driven by differential land-sea heating, the ITCZ shift, the Tibetan Plateau heating, and the **tropical easterly & subtropical westerly jets**; **El Niño/La Niña (ENSO)** and the **Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)** modulate its strength.
**Special phenomena (the exam set):** cyclones (Bay of Bengal is highly cyclogenic — directly relevant to AP), western disturbances, cloudbursts, El Niño, jet streams, and monsoon 'break'.
**AP relevance:** the state's climate is governed by the SW monsoon (June-Sep) and the retreating NE monsoon (Oct-Dec, vital for coastal AP & Rayalaseema).

prelimsPointers: **ITCZ, ENSO (El Niño/La Niña) and the Indian Ocean Dipole** modulate the Indian monsoon.
Coastal Andhra receives significant rain from the **retreating/NE monsoon** (Oct-Dec).
Normal **lapse rate ~6.5°C/km**; inversion = temperature rising with height (frost hollows, smog lids).
**Relative humidity** peaks near dawn; dew point = saturation temperature; ~**7% more vapour per °C** warming.
Cloud families: **cirro- (high, ice), alto- (mid), strato-/nimbo- (low), cumulo- (vertical)**; cumulonimbus → thunder, hail, tornado.
**Coriolis zero at the equator** — hence no cyclones within ~5° latitude; deflection right in NH.
Monsoon jets: **Somali/Findlater (low-level, cross-equatorial)** & **Tropical Easterly Jet (upper, 100-150 hPa)**; **western disturbances** = winter's extra-tropical rain in NW India.
**El Niño**: warm eastern Pacific ↔ weakened Walker cell ↔ Indian-monsoon deficit tendency; **positive IOD** compensates.
**NE (retreating) monsoon (Oct-Dec)** is the principal wet season for **south-coastal AP & Rayalaseema**; Bay cyclones cluster **Oct-Nov**.
**Lightning kills ~2,500+ Indians yearly** — the largest single weather cause of death.

glossary.definition: Warm air overlying cold, suppressing convection — the lid that traps smog and frost.
Actual vapour as a percentage of the air's saturation capacity at that temperature — the comfort and condensation index.
The equatorial convergence-rainfall belt whose seasonal migration drives the monsoon's advance and retreat.
Narrow bands of very fast upper-tropospheric winds steering weather systems — India's monsoon dances with the STWJ and TEJ.
Mediterranean-origin extra-tropical systems bringing winter rain-snow to northwest India — rabi's benefactor.
Cyclone-driven sea-level upheaval flooding coasts — the deadliest limb of Bay of Bengal cyclones.

rows: Plate-boundary strain release (Himalayan thrust — the great-quake deficit); **zones II-V (IS 1893)**; intraplate surprises (Latur 1993, Bhuj 2001 — Zone V pocket)

AP mostly **Zone II-III** (low-moderate); Ongole-coastal Zone III strips; reservoir-linked tremors debated (Srisailam environs) — AP's real seismic file is **building-code compliance**, not fault lines
Slope + saturation + seismicity + slope-cutting; Himalaya & Western Ghats as the twin belts (Wayanad 2024 the recent tragedy)
Eastern Ghats' modest but real slides — **Araku-Visakhapatnam agency road cuts**, 2020s ghat-road failures; mining-destabilised slopes

Riverine (basin monsoal peaks), flash (cloudbursts, urban), coastal (surge); Brahmaputra-Ganga plains the national theatre; **urban flooding** the new normal (encroached drains + C-C rainfall intensification)

**Godavari's fury** (2022's ~26 lakh cusecs at Bhadrachalam-Polavaram reach; Konaseema inundation), **Krishna 2009** (Kurnool submerged — Srisailam backwater), **Budameru's Vijayawada flood (Sept 2024** — the city's worst in decades), Pennar flash events
Bay of Bengal = the world's deadliest basin (shallow shelf → surge amplification; funnel geometry); Oct-Nov + May windows

**AP = cyclone alley**: 1977 Diviseema (~10,000+ dead — the trauma benchmark), 1990 Machilipatnam, 1996 Godavari, **Hudhud 2014 (Visakhapatnam — a city hit head-on; ~₹22,000 cr damage)**, Titli 2018 (Srikakulam), Michaung 2023 (flooding Nellore-Tirupati belts) — the improvement arc: 10,000 dead (1977) → double digits (Hudhud) → near-zero: the zero-casualty doctrine
**Cloudbursts (+ heat & drought as the quiet hazards)**
Cloudburst: >10 cm/hour convective dumps, Himalayan valleys' speciality; heatwaves & drought as slow killers
AP's analogue: intense convective bursts on ghat towns; **heatwaves** (2015's ~1,700+ AP deaths — among India's worst) and **Rayalaseema's chronic drought** — the hazards without sirens

items: **Hazard ≠ disaster**: risk = hazard × exposure × vulnerability ÷ capacity — the framing equation; India's curve shows hazards constant-to-worsening (climate) while **mortality falls where capacity rose** (cyclones) and rises where exposure grew unplanned (urban floods, heat).

**Climate-change multipliers**: rapid-intensification cyclones (warmer bay), C-C rainfall extremes (urban flash floods), compound events (surge + river flood — Godavari-cyclone coincidences), longer heatwaves — attribute carefully ('consistent with' language).

**The AP arc as the answer's spine**: 1977 Diviseema's trauma → cyclone shelters + IMD radar net + evacuation drill culture → **Hudhud's single-city test** → zero-casualty playbook (early warning to the last fisherman via secretariat-volunteer capillaries) — the world-cited success; against it, the **new deficits**: Budameru's urban-drainage failure, heat-action gaps, drought's quiet attrition — success in the siren hazards, homework in the silent ones.

sections.heading: 🗺 Deep mastery — hazard anatomy, five files

rows: High — the AP coast is among India's most cyclone-prone

items: **Cross-cutting:** vulnerability = hazard × exposure × (–coping capacity); the shift from **relief to risk reduction (Sendai, NDMA)**.
**AP's model:** early-warning (IMD/INCOIS), cyclone shelters, and near-zero-casualty evacuations — a national reference in disaster preparedness.

prelimsPointers: The **Bay of Bengal** is more cyclogenic than the Arabian Sea; AP & Odisha are highly exposed.
**INCOIS (Hyderabad)** provides tsunami/storm-surge early warnings for the AP coast.
India's seismic zoning (IS 1893): **Zones II-V**; ~59% of area quake-prone; AP largely **Zone II-III**.
**Diviseema cyclone (19 Nov 1977)**: ~10,000+ deaths in the Krishna delta — AP's disaster benchmark.
**Hudhud (12 Oct 2014)** made landfall at **Visakhapatnam** — rare direct city hit; ~₹22,000 crore damage, casualties held to double digits.
**Krishna floods 2009** submerged Kurnool; **Godavari 2022** neared record flows at the Polavaram reach; **Budameru overflow flooded Vijayawada, Sept 2024**.
**2015 heatwave** killed ~1,700+ in AP — among India's deadliest heat events.
Bay of Bengal's lethality: shallow shelf + funnel = **surge amplification**; world's deadliest cyclone basin.
**Cloudburst** definition: ~**100 mm/hour** over a small area.
Risk equation: **hazard × exposure × vulnerability ÷ capacity**.

glossary.definition: The susceptibility of people and assets to hazard harm — poverty, housing quality, age, location as its determinants.
Cyclone-driven coastal sea rise — the Bay's shallow shelf amplifies it into the basin's deadliest weapon.
A cyclone's swift strengthening (≥30 kt/24 h) over warm waters — the forecast-challenging climate-era trend.
Sudden high-intensity flood from cloudbursts or dam-drain failure — minutes-to-hours lead time.
Co-occurring hazards (surge + riverine flood, heat + drought) whose joint impact exceeds their sum.
AP-Odisha's evacuation-first cyclone protocol — warning, shelters and last-mile drill aiming at no deaths.
